title: Domain-Adapted Small Language Models for Reliable Clinical Triage
abstract: arXiv:2604.26766v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Accurate and consistent Emergency Severity Index (ESI) assignment remains a persistent challenge in emergency departments, where highly variable free-text triage documentation contributes to mistriage and workflow inefficiencies. This study evaluates whether open-source small language models (SLMs) can serve as reliable, privacy-preserving decision-support tools for clinical triage. translated_title: 面向可靠临床分诊的领域适配小语言模型
translated_abstract: 准确且一致地分配急诊严重程度指数（ESI）分级仍然是急诊科面临的持续性挑战，高度多变的自由文本分诊记录会导致误分诊和工作流程低效。本研究评估了开源小语言模型（SLMs）能否作为可靠且保护隐私的临床分诊决策支持工具。我们系统比较了多个SLM在不同提示流程下的表现，发现临床病例摘要（即分诊叙述的简明总结）能够产生最准确的预测。其中，Qwen2.5-7B在准确性、稳定性和计算效率之间展现出最佳平衡。通过利用专家整理和银标准的儿科分诊数据进行大规模领域适配，微调后的Qwen2.5-7B模型显著降低了分级不一致性和具有临床意义的错误，其表现优于所有基线SLM和先进的专有模型。
tldr: 该研究通过专家儿科分诊数据对开源小语言模型Qwen2.5-7B进行领域适配微调，显著减少误分诊和临床重大错误，其性能超越基线模型和先进专有模型，可作为可靠且保护隐私的临床分诊决策支持工具。
en_tdlr: This study demonstrates that domain-adapted fine-tuning of the open-source small language model Qwen2.5-7B on expert-curated pediatric triage data substantially reduces discordance and clinically significant errors, outperforming baseline SLMs and proprietary models as a reliable, privacy-preserving clinical triage decision-support tool.
